prose.source: The verification state of an issue's acceptance criteria: what each criterion's instrument reported, against which revision, and which criteria that evidence lets a body tick.
Read these files first.
- [Issue Body](issue-body.md)
- [Epic Issue Body](epic-issue-body.md)
- [Initiative Issue Body](initiative-issue-body.md)
The verification evidence for a supplied set of criteria whose delivery is ready.
1. Confirm the supplied delivery findings establish [Readiness](#readiness) for each selected criterion.
- Return evidence that fails Readiness as a blocker for that criterion.
2. Run each criterion's named instrument at the delivering pull request head for an open task, or its merged revision for delivered work, meeting [Instrument Checkout](#instrument-checkout).
- Run [Run at Revision](#run-at-revision) with the project checkout, that revision and the instrument.
- Record the result against the commit it reports, meeting [Instrument Result](#instrument-result).
3. Return verified criterion ids with their evidence and each unresolved criterion with what is missing.
- Leave body publication and further planning to the caller.
The confirmed criteria and completed rows recorded in an epic or initiative body.
1. Record the criteria, meeting [Tick State](#tick-state).

- For an epic, run [Record Epic Criteria](epic-issue-body.md#record-epic-criteria) with the issue JSON, pull request records, complete issue-link snapshot, verified criterion ids and output body file.
- For an initiative, run [Record Initiative Criteria](initiative-issue-body.md#record-initiative-criteria) with the issue JSON, every linked epic record, verified criterion ids and output body file.
2. Return the resulting body and any refused criteria to the caller for publication.
- **Criterion.** The id of one acceptance criterion in the issue body that states it.
- **Instrument.** The command, test or check the criterion names as the thing that observes it.
- **Revision.**
The exact commit the instrument ran against: the open task pull request head or the delivered revision in its target branch.

A task criterion is ready to verify when its delivering pull request, open or merged, supplies readable evidence at the revision being checked. Epic criteria require their delivering rows to be delivered. An unreadable dependency leaves a criterion unready; tracker closure requires merged delivery.

An instrument runs in a checkout of the project at the exact revision it is verifying, which the caller supplies. A checkout the caller is editing is not that revision, so a criterion verified against uncommitted work is unverified. A branch or tag is resolved to one commit before the run, and the checkout made for the run is removed after it whatever the instrument returns.

A criterion is verified only on a passing run of its named instrument, recorded against the tested revisions as [Coverage Reports](issue-body.md#coverage-reports) define. A failed, unavailable or inconclusive instrument leaves it unverified, and an unverified criterion is not ticked.

A ticked criterion carries verification evidence. Epic criteria can derive that evidence from passed checks under [Test Evidence](epic-issue-body.md#test-evidence). Done on the row or table that cites it follows [Tables](issue-body.md#tables) and [Work Breakdown](epic-issue-body.md#work-breakdown). A criterion refused as not ready to verify is returned unticked with what it is missing.
Runs one instrument at the commit a branch, tag or commit resolves to, in a detached checkout the run creates and removes.
- `--project` is any checkout of the repository; `--revision` is the branch, tag or commit under verification. The instrument follows `--` and runs at the checkout's top level.
- The first output line is `{"revision": <commit>, "checkout": <path>}`, the commit the result is recorded against. The instrument's output follows.
- The exit status is the instrument's, whatever it is. The checkout is removed after a pass or a failure; one it cannot remove is reported with its path and the instrument's status stands.

- Exit 125 is the helper's own failure, as `git bisect run` reserves it, with one standard error line naming the cause: a usage error, `revision not found:` or `checkout not created:` before any output, or `command not started:` after the first line, once the checkout exists. An instrument that itself exits 125 is told apart by that line's absence.
- Worktrees the run did not create are left as they are.

- The checkout is registered in the repository's git directory, which `sbx` leaves read-only for a linked worktree or another repository, so the helper runs outside `sbx`. An instrument that needs the sandbox carries its own `sbx` prefix.
**Example:**
An epic's prerequisite evidence, task delivery findings, integration readiness and completion state.
Read these files first.
- [Initiative Issue Body](initiative-issue-body.md)
- [Issue](issue.md)
The evidence required before starting an epic's work.
1. Identify each prerequisite the supplied initiative row names.
2. Apply the initiative's [whole-epic dependency rule](initiative-issue-body.md#work-breakdown); a task row's reference to a row of another epic gates that row rather than this epic.
3. Confirm each prerequisite epic is closed as completed and every one of its bases has merged. Missing records leave the prerequisite unconfirmed.

4. Return the [Prerequisite Evidence](#prerequisite-evidence), identifying each confirmed prerequisite and missing condition. Only a confirmed result permits an unstarted epic's bases to be created or its task to be dispatched.
The delivery findings for one epic from supplied evidence.
1. Run [Match Pull Requests](#match-pull-requests) with the epic JSON, pull request records as `--prs` and link snapshot as `--links`, supplying a local scratch output body as `--fix`.
- A closed epic is normalized to the current Work Breakdown columns before its tasks are read, using the shared format rules. Ambiguous or unsupported table content is a blocker.
- Publish reported table normalization through [Save Tracker Issue](issue.md#save-tracker-issue), fetch the saved epic and repeat the match before returning its evidence.
2. Return the [Delivery Findings](#delivery-findings); missing linked pull requests are missing evidence for the caller to supply.
The epic's eligibility for integration from current delivery and criterion evidence.
1. Run [Inspect Epic Delivery](#inspect-epic-delivery) with the supplied epic JSON, pull request records and complete issue-link snapshot.

2. Confirm every task is delivered, every epic criterion is verified and ticked, and no open question or unresolved delivery discrepancy remains. An unmerged epic base awaiting integration is expected at this stage. Missing or stale verification leaves readiness unconfirmed.

3. Return the integration readiness in [Delivery State](#delivery-state), with the evidence revisions and each blocker. Readiness establishes the epic's content conditions; the caller supplies pull-request review, target and head-check evidence for the merge.
The epic's normal delivery result before tracker closure.
1. Run [Check Epic Readiness](#check-epic-readiness) with the current epic, pull request records, issue-link snapshot and criterion verification evidence.
2. Reconcile the expected bases with the task delivery targets.

3. Confirm every base has merged into its corresponding long-lived branch. An unknown or incomplete base list, or missing merge evidence, leaves completion unconfirmed even when every task is delivered and every criterion is ticked.

4. Return the completion result in [Delivery State](#delivery-state), identifying remaining blockers. Passing normal delivery checks supplies the caller's closure evidence; the tracker issue's current Development-link gate still governs the write.
Each prerequisite has its issue identity and completion state, expected delivery bases and their merge evidence. The result identifies confirmed and missing conditions for the candidate epic.

The epic is identified by its repository and issue number. Its state contains task delivery findings, criterion verification and ticks, open questions, expected delivery bases and their merges, and the revisions supporting the evidence. Integration readiness and completion are separate results, each with its unresolved conditions. An epic may be ready to integrate while one or more bases await merging.
| Line | What it names |
| Normalized | Closed-epic table corrections present in the output body. |

| Retitle | A merged pull request linked by a task row whose title has no prefix or only a matching initiative or task prefix, or any pull request whose title names an epic of the initiative by a task id, with the required title for publication and readback. |
| Conflict | Tasks that share a pull request and do not name each other in Joins. A row linked to a pull request whose title names another epic. |
| Unmatched | A merged pull request that names the epic and that no row links. |
| In flight | An open pull request that names the epic and that no row links. A pull request whose head is an epic base is not a task match. |

| Draft | An epic base a merged task targets that holds a commit its long-lived branch lacks and has no open pull request merging it, while a task is undelivered or a criterion is unticked. A base level with or behind its branch is not draft. |
| Unmerged | An epic base its pull requests target that has not merged into its long-lived branch, once every task is delivered and every criterion is ticked. A draft pull request is named draft. |
| References | A review pull request whose cited pull requests differ from the task pull requests merged into its base. |

| Changes | A review pull request whose Changes section names, in a code span, a file absent from the head commit of the base it fronts, with that span. A span, less any `#anchor` or `:line` suffix, names a path when it holds a directory and carries an extension or opens with a top-level directory of that head, or is a bare name whose extension a file at that head carries; a component `<branch>:<path>` names its path only for the base of that branch. A path stands where the head holds a file or a directory at it. |
| Uncited | A linked pull request whose task has its own issue and does not link it, or a review pull request that does not link the epic's issue. |
| Note | A row that links its task issue. |
| Unchanged | A row that links a task issue the run was not given. Its Done cell stands, and the epic is not closable until a run is given that issue. |
| Unplaced | A task issue of this epic whose id is not a row. |
| Open questions | The epic's Open Questions section remains. |
| Ready to verify | An unticked criterion whose delivering rows are all delivered and whose linked passed checks do not settle it. |
| Ticked early | A criterion ticked while a delivering row is not delivered. |
| Disagreement | A linked pull request's test plan against the Coverage of the rows it delivers. |

| Target | An open or merged pull request naming the epic off its delivery routes: a task pull request into anything but one of the epic's bases, or an integration pull request into anything but the long-lived branch its head names. Each names the base it belongs in: for a task pull request, the epic base of the long-lived branch its task branch's last slug word names where another of the epic's pull requests comes from a branch of the same stem ending in another long-lived branch, as a unit changing several takes one task branch per base; else of the one its target names; else each epic base as one of them. |

| No epic | A pull request whose title opens with the initiative's id, `[I07`, and names neither an epic as `[I07:E00]` nor a task as `[I07:E00:W01]`: a bare `[I07]`, or an epic id in any other form, such as `[I07:E1]`. Nothing reads it as delivery. |
| Source | The configuration path, commit and repository of each `config/branches` statement the long-lived branch names were read from. |

| Unevaluable | A `config/branches` statement that is absent, empty or unreadable at its epic base, or a revision resolving to no commit, with its source; statements that disagree across the epic bases, each with its source and names; no long-lived branches given; a base that would be draft whose commits cannot be compared with its long-lived branch; or a review whose head commit the checkout does not hold, so its Changes paths are unread; each with the reason. |
| Not checked | Each epic check that reads the long-lived branches, while their names are unevaluable. |

An unmet row links a merged pull request while a covered criterion remains unticked. A linked pull request naming another epic is a conflict and delivers its linked task once merged. A missing linked pull request leaves the supplied evidence incomplete.

A coverage disagreement identifies the pull request and row, a criterion absent from either the test plan or row Coverage, an empty Test cell, or prose assigning the criterion to another task. Recording links, verified criteria and Done continues despite that finding.
Reports an epic's delivery state against the pull requests that name it.
- Results follow [Delivery Findings](#delivery-findings).
**Example:**

Check Epic Completion.inputs: **Inputs:** [Epic Record](#epic-record), [Pull Request Records](#pull-request-records), [Issue Links](#issue-links), [Verification Evidence](#verification-evidence), [Base Merges](#base-merges).

prose.source: Populates one epic body. The body states one slice of the design and lists the tasks that deliver it.
Read these files first.
- [Lane](lane.md)
- [Issue Body](issue-body.md)
- [Pull Request](pull-request.md)
- [Epic](epic.md)
- [Issue](issue.md)
- [Dependency Graph](dependency-graph.md)
- [Delivery Plan](delivery-plan.md)
One epic body and its local validation findings.
1. Populate the body from the [Template](#template) at the supplied output path.
- Every section must meet [Fields](#fields).
- Shared content must meet the common [body conditions](issue-body.md#fields).
2. Populate the shared table through [Write Issue Table](issue-body.md#write-issue-table).
3. Fill the epic-specific cells.
- Each row must meet [Work Breakdown](#work-breakdown).
- Call [Assign Task Lanes](lane.md#assign-task-lanes) with the populated body, confirmed task-to-index map and output path.
4. Call [Build Body Snapshot](issue-body.md#build-body-snapshot) with the draft body, title, labels and existing issue JSON when present.
5. Pass that snapshot, initiative context, available pull request records, project checkout, evaluated revision and output file to [Validate Epic Body](#validate-epic-body).
6. Identify unresolved publication links separately; they remain pending until tracker identities exist.
7. Return the draft rows, their dependency references and the validation findings for the caller's cross-body ordering check.
One epic body with supplied delivery matches and completed rows recorded.

1. Run [Sync Epic](#sync-epic), mapping pull requests to `--prs`, links to `--links`, task issues to `--tasks`, each confirmed match to `--link`, the checkout to `--project`, each fetched epic base to a `--revision` and the output file to `--fix`.
- Row changes must meet [Task Delivery](#task-delivery) and [Work Breakdown](#work-breakdown).
2. Return the updated body and [Delivery Findings](epic.md#delivery-findings) for the caller to resolve and publish. An unmerged epic base prevents a closable result.
Verified criteria and completed rows in one epic body.
1. Run [Tick Epic Criteria](#tick-epic-criteria) with the epic JSON, records as `--prs`, snapshot as `--links`, verified ids as `--tick` and output as `--fix`. Refuse criteria not ready to verify.
2. Return the body and refused criteria.
Task rows held for one confirmed delivery session.

1. Require the caller's confirmed unit and existing planning folder. Refuse a row already held or linked to a pull request or commit, and a unit [Work Units](delivery-plan.md#work-units) does not admit.

2. Run [Reserve Row](#reserve-row) with the epic as `--epic`, every id of the unit as `--reserve`, the board items as `--items`, supplied base URL as `--records`, record date as `--date` and output as `--fix`.
3. Return the reserved body meeting [Task Delivery](#task-delivery).
Held task rows returned to their work-item links.
1. Require the supplied release decision and refuse any row that is not held.
2. Run [Release Row](#release-row) with the epic as `--epic`, every id of each released unit as `--release`, the engineering worktree as `--engineering` and output as `--fix`.
3. Return the released body meeting [Task Delivery](#task-delivery).
The body's local format and field findings.

1. Read the changed paths of each epic pull request reaching a branch the project's [Required Criteria](#required-criteria) declare, through [Read Pull Request State](pull-request.md#read-pull-request-state).

2. Call [Validate Issue Body](issue-body.md#validate-issue-body) with the current body, local [Fields](#fields), supplied related evidence and output file, supplying initiative JSON as `--initiative`, pull requests as `--prs`, each pull request's changed paths as `--files <number>=<changed-paths-file>`, the checkout as `--project` and the revision as `--revision`.

- The evaluated revision is the epic's base on the long-lived branch that holds the project's configuration, such as `origin/i07/e00/workspace`, or that branch itself, such as `origin/workspace`, while the epic has no base on it. Fetch it before the check reads it.
3. Read reach from each epic pull request's base, through an epic base or initiative branch. Without pull requests, no criterion is lacking.

4. Include in the findings each [Required Criteria](#required-criteria) criterion an epic lacks whose work changes the criterion's paths on its branch, required criteria the declaration or the changed paths leave unevaluable, and any epic criterion no task row delivers.
5. Return the corrected body, mechanical diff and unresolved findings for the caller.
One epic body with confirmed task-grain and coverage corrections.
1. Apply the confirmed row changes through [Populate Epic Issue Body](#populate-epic-issue-body), preserving unrelated content.
- Description, Coverage, Depends on, Joins, Lane and task grain must meet [Work Breakdown](#work-breakdown).
- Split a task exceeding the allowed criterion grain into the confirmed tasks.
2. Return the revised body and any cross-body numbering or dependency changes for the caller.
The agreed disposition of criteria a delivered row left unmet.
1. Present each unmet criterion and its missing evidence to the user.
- Return the criteria the user confirms already hold to the caller for verification and ticking. The delivered task retains them.
- Record an unanswered decision as pending.
- If no criteria need further work, return the pending findings to the caller.
- Continue to the draft step with only the criteria the user confirms need further work.
2. Draft a further task for the criteria selected for further work, meeting [Work Breakdown](#work-breakdown).
- Confirm the draft with the user.
- On acceptance, call [Revise Epic Rows](#revise-epic-rows) with the further row and the criteria it adopts from the delivered task's Coverage.
- Return an unanswered draft as pending without continuing to the reconcile step.
3. Run [Record Epic Delivery](#record-epic-delivery) with the revised epic, the supplied delivery evidence, the project checkout and the fetched epic bases.
- Publish the returned body through [Save Tracker Issue](issue.md#save-tracker-issue).
- Return the saved row and criterion disposition to the caller.
- The title is `[I07:E00] Name: Subtitle`. Its prefix matches its row in the initiative table.
- Labels are `type:epic` and its initiative's `theme:*`.
- `E` is the epic within its initiative. Epics count from `00`.
- The prefix separates levels with colons, then a short name, a colon, and a subtitle: `[I07:E06] Reliability Evaluation: Briefs, Measures and the Thresholds That Define Reliable`.
- A boundary with a sibling epic is plain language.

New tasks exist as epic rows with their details, discussion and evidence in the epic and planning record. Planning creates no separate task issues. Existing issues hoisted into an epic retain their records and row links when new tasks are planned.
The columns are `Task | Description | Coverage | Depends on | Joins | Lane | Done`.
- **Done.**
A task row is complete when it is delivered, and every criterion its Coverage names is ticked.
- **Row id.**
The row id is the task, `W01`. `W00` holds preparatory work that must land before the first real task.
- **Description.**
Each detail beyond the phrase is a criterion stating one invariant.
- **Coverage.**

Coverage names the epic's criteria the task delivers, whether its Done cell is ticked or empty. Each row claims only criteria its work makes true; it cannot claim a criterion another row delivers alone or one its work cannot meet. A cell is empty only on a delivered task whose criteria a further task adopts, as task grain states.
- **Depends on.**
A task row names the rows it depends on. An earlier task in the epic (`W03`, `W04–W09`), a row of an earlier epic (`[E01:W02](…)`), or something outside the initiative (`#750`, `[I05:E00:W02](…)`).

- A task row names rows, never an epic. It names the row producing each output it consumes (`[E01:W01](…), [E01:W02](…)`), and where the task consumes from every row of an epic that is what establishes the whole-epic reach.
- Cross-epic dependencies name rows before any issue of the epic is created. Both tables exist, and each edge names the row that produces what the dependent row consumes.
- A dependency listed twice or already implied by another in the cell is unsound. A task that measures, extends or consumes another task's output depends on it, even when the prose does not say so.
- **Task grain.**
- A task is one pull request's worth of work.

- A criterion a merged pull request left unticked belongs to a further task. The further task depends on the delivered task, and its Coverage is that criterion. Criteria one pull request can deliver share one further task. The delivered task's Coverage omits each criterion a further task adopts.
- A task delivering more than three criteria is split into tasks one pull request each can deliver.

- A task covers at least one acceptance criterion. A criterion more than one row cites is imprecise: it is split into the invariant each task makes true, and each is cited from the row that delivers it.

- Every test the work calls for accompanies that task. The content steers which kinds those are, including the project's system test when the work is something that test can exercise. A failure in any test the task carries keeps the task open. None of those tests is a later row.
- Reusable routines, techniques, and resources are specced, created, and tested before an activity binds them. The grain of an existing resource is in that work.

- When the behaviour a wired activity produces differs from the behaviour the work expected, that task changes the routine, technique, or resource, and the tests that cover the change, until fit, form, and function hold.
- **Joins.**
The tasks that share one pull request. Two tasks sharing one name each other, and tasks linked by such pairs are one joined unit.
- A joined unit holds no Depends on between its members: the pull request orders their commits.
- Only a path between two members through a task outside the unit bars a join.
- A joined unit covers at most six criteria, two full rows' worth, so it stays one pull request's worth.
- Joins are complete before any issue of the epic is created. Each candidate unit, the rows declaring one component, is answered as [Joins](dependency-graph.md#joins) states.
- An empty cell is a task that shares no pull request.
- **Lane.**
The row's delivery lane meets [Assignments](lane.md#assignments).
- **Numbering.**
Task numbering meets [Numbering](issue-body.md#numbering); a row whose id links a pull request is fixed.
- **Reference form.**
A table reference uses colons (`E01:W03`, `I05:E00:W02`), and every epic reference links to that epic's issue: `[E01:W03](…/issues/937)`. Prose uses a space (`E01 W03`).

A criterion receives an automatic tick when every task covering it is delivered and supplies an observing check in its linked pull requests. Every observing check must pass in a merged pull request; absent records, unreadable plans and incomplete checks supply no verification. Evidence applies only to the linked task's Coverage. Existing ticks are preserved, and explicitly verified criteria remain subject to delivery readiness.
An epic criterion meets the [shared acceptance criteria](issue-body.md#shared-acceptance-criteria). Contradictions between criteria in one epic are findings.
Each question holds only what is undecided and has a recommendation in the planning record. A settled point belongs in that record. No question remains when the epic starts.

A project states the criteria its epics must carry in `config/required-criteria.json` at its root. The file is a JSON array, and each entry is one required criterion with these fields, each a non-empty string except `paths`:
| Field | What it states |
| `branch` | The long-lived branch the criterion's work reaches. |

| `paths` | A non-empty list of files and directories on `branch`. An epic carries the criterion when a pull request of its work reaching `branch` changes a file that is one of them or lies under one. |
| `criterion` | The criterion's text, which the epic carries after its `**ACn.**` label. |
| `phrase` | A phrase identifying the criterion in an epic that carries it, matched without regard to case. |
| `row` | The Description of the task row that delivers the criterion. |
- **The declared row delivers the criterion.**
It carries the declared `row` as its Description, depends on the rows whose work changes the declared paths, and covers that criterion alone.
- **The tracker states what the work changes.**

The check reads each pull request's changed files as the tracker lists them. A pull request reaching the declared branch whose changed files are not supplied leaves the criterion unevaluable, unless another pull request of the epic is known to change a declared path.
- **The evaluated commit holds the statement.**

The check reads the file at the commit its evaluated revision resolves to, in the repository its checkout locates, and names that path, commit and repository as its source. Which worktree the checkout is, and what its working files hold, choose nothing.
- **A project declaring nothing requires nothing.**
A missing or empty file at the evaluated commit, or an empty array, declares no required criterion, and the check reports none. A project declaring nothing acquires no other project's criteria.
- **An unreadable statement is unevaluable.**

A revision resolving to no commit, unreadable JSON, a value other than an array, or an entry lacking a field or stating `paths` as anything but a non-empty list of non-empty strings leaves the project's required criteria unevaluable. The check reports that and names the fault, and reports no epic as lacking a criterion.
- **Example.**
workflow-server requires its corpus audit of work that changes the workflow definitions under `corpus` on `workflows`:
- **Task ids.**
- An unreserved task awaiting its pull request links its file in the planning record: `[W01](…/w01.md)`. The file name is the task id in lower case.

- Every link on a task row names that row's id, and the row carries one delivery per long-lived branch its unit changes. A reserved task links only its planning folder: `[W01](…/2026-10-06-943-i07-e00-w01-queue-plan/)`. Every row of a joined unit links the one folder its first row names. The folder's README links each work-item file by the name the row's link carries. Releasing the reservation points the row to that file.

- Once a pull request is open, its link replaces the planning link: `[W01](…/pull/950)`. A unit changing two long-lived branches links the pull request on each: `[W01](…/pull/950), [W01](…/pull/951)`. Further delivery work on one of those branches gets another task row under Task grain. Joined rows each link their shared pull request.
- The task is delivered when a linked pull request has merged, or its id links a commit.
- A link to an open pull request does not deliver the task.
- A linked pull request whose title names another epic delivers the task once it has merged. The mismatch is reported, and the row stays open while a criterion its Coverage names is unticked.
- **Tasks with their own issue.**
- A task issue belongs to one epic. Its title carries that epic's prefix.
- When that epic's table has no row for its id, the issue is unplaced. Once the row exists, that epic's planning manages the issue.
- The row links the pull request, not the issue.
- The pull request's Development field links the issue as [Issue Links](pull-request.md#issue-links) state.
- A completed task issue has all criteria verified and every Development-linked pull request merged.
- **Issues backing several tasks.**
An issue backing several tasks, such as an investigation, is a reference: the epic cites it under References, no row id links it, and its title carries no agent-engineering prefix.
- **Work another issue takes.**
It leaves the table. Its criteria go with it, or to another row that delivers them.
Work Breakdown contains its table. Explanatory prose belongs in Proposal. The body does not narrate execution order or how the tables work; Depends on carries the order.
Links each named task's id to the pull requests naming the epic it is delivered through, open or merged, and ticks Done on a row once it is complete.
- A row whose id links its task issue links the pull request instead.
- A pull request whose head is an epic base is the pull request that merges that base, and is not matched to a task.
- An unmerged epic base keeps the epic open, even when every row is delivered and every criterion is ticked.

- An epic base is reported `draft` only where it holds a commit its long-lived branch lacks. The base is read at the `--revision` naming it and the long-lived branch beside it on the same remote, so `origin/i07/e00/main` is compared with `origin/main`; a base no `--revision` names is reported `unevaluable`.

- `--project` is a checkout of the project and each `--revision` one of the epic's bases, such as `origin/i07/e00/main`. The long-lived branch names are the ones `config/branches` states at those commits, and each `source` line names a path, commit and repository.

- An absent, empty or unreadable statement, and statements that disagree across the bases, are reported `unevaluable` with their source. Without the long-lived branch names, the run names each check it did not make as `not checked`, and an epic that would otherwise be closable is not.

- An open review pull request's Changes paths are read at its head commit in the `--project` repository: a path with a directory stands where the head holds a file or a directory at it, and a bare file name anywhere in the tree. A head commit the repository does not hold is reported `unevaluable`.
- Passed checks settle criteria under [Test Evidence](#test-evidence).

- `--link` names each task id and the pull request number it links. An id repeats once for each pull request, one per long-lived branch its unit changes. The row keeps the deliveries it links in place and gains each named one it lacks, so a repeated run leaves it unchanged. `--tasks` is the task issues. `--links` is the pull requests' Development-linked issues. `--fix` is the body written with the Done ticks.

`<task-pull-request-map>` is a comma-separated list of `<task-id>=<pull-request-number>` pairs, with a pair for each pull request a task id links. Pass each task JSON file as a separate argument after `--tasks`.
**Example:**
Ticks confirmed epic criteria, refusing any not ready to verify, and ticks completed rows.
`<criterion-ids>` is a comma-separated list of verified criterion ids.
**Example:**
Holds each named unit for one session, by setting its record folder as the single link of every row in it.
- `--items` is the board's items with Status.
- `--records` is the URL of the planning records folder, needed when no row id in the epic links a record.
- The caller supplies the planned folder identity; `--date` is the day it is opened.
- The folder is the one the unit's first task id and Description give it, as the available-work report's `unit` line names it. A call naming some rows of a joined unit and not the others is refused.
`<task-ids>` is a comma-separated list of task ids; `<records-base-url>` identifies the planning records folder.
**Example:**
Frees each named task row, by replacing the planning-folder link with its work-item file link.
- The file is the task id in lowercase within that folder, as [Task ids](#task-delivery) defines.
- `--engineering` is the checkout holding the planning records. A row whose folder there holds no such file, or whose README does not link it, is refused.
- A call naming some rows of a joined unit and not the others is refused.

Any open pull request whose Development field links it, draft or not, makes it running: it is neither offered nor released, and an In Progress status it holds stays its hold. - **Unrecorded.**

The columns are `Epic | Description | Coverage | Depends on | Done`. The table has no Joins column.
- An epic row's id is the epic, linked to its issue: `[E01](…/issues/937)`.
- An epic row's Description is the epic's title name, and its Coverage names the initiative criteria the epic serves.
- An epic row is complete when its issue is closed as completed.

- An epic row whose issue is closed as not planned leaves the table. Each criterion only that row covers leaves with it, and a criterion another row also covers stays. The criteria that remain keep their [labels](issue-body.md#criterion-labels).

- Depends on names epics only. A cell that names a task fails. Name a prerequisite epic only when every task or joined unit in the dependent epic requires every task in that prerequisite epic, directly or through its dependencies. The consumed output and the work producing it establish that requirement. Dependencies on selected tasks remain in the task tables. An edge another named whole-epic prerequisite already implies is omitted.
- An initiative dependency that only some tasks need, or that requires only part of its prerequisite epic, is overbroad. The output and its producing tasks establish the edge.
- An epic depending on a later epic is a backward reference.

An initiative criterion meets the [shared acceptance criteria](issue-body.md#shared-acceptance-criteria) and [Requirement Characteristics](../references/requirement-characteristics.md), and:
- **No counts.**

An initiative criterion carries no counts or figures, which go stale: it measures against a named baseline or check ("against the baseline", "as the budget test measures it"). A figure stays only where it is the criterion's own target, such as a bound it holds to.
- **SMART.**

Each initiative criterion is specific about what holds, measurable by a named check or baseline, achievable by the epics that cite it, and relevant, tracing to a clause and to the Problem. It is time-bound by a release tag or another named milestone outside the initiative's own work, where one exists, and otherwise by the epics that cite it.
- **Local.**

An initiative criterion names no initiative, epic, task or issue, and is solution-agnostic. Coverage cells link epics to criteria. One that holds only through another initiative's work is restated as what this initiative achieves, or it is dropped.
- **Whole.**

An initiative criterion states what the initiative achieves as a whole. One that restates a single epic's criterion is a duplicate: it is raised to what the epics achieve together, or left to the epic.
- **Verified.**
- An initiative criterion ends by naming its instrument. Which instruments keep a criterion is [Verifiable](issue-body.md#verifiable).

- An automated test is an end-to-end walk through the real server, a smoke run of an agent against a live server, a live check on a deployed host, or a guard, fixture suite or check that continuous integration runs. The walk, smoke run or live check is preferred where the criterion is about what a run does.

- A named test that does not exist yet is work the plan holds: a task in the epic whose subject it tests, or a discrete test-infrastructure epic when the tests serve several criteria. That epic's row cites the criteria its tests verify.
- One succinct sentence each on what the initiative does not do, naming no initiative, epic, task or issue, and no owner.
- A proposal-derived initiative identifies its originating proposal in References with the proposal's exact title and issue URL, labelled as the originating proposal.

- A reference the criteria answer to carries **Source.** after its label: `- **R1.** **Source.** [Title](url) — what it binds`. An unmarked reference is background, and binds no criterion. What a marked one requires of the criteria is [Sources](#sources).
- A cross-initiative overlap is recorded in References. An approved edit to another initiative's issue stays minimal.
- An initiative that removes a not-planned epic's row carries a reference linking the issue that takes that epic's work.
A marked source in References is a document the initiative's criteria answer to. The criteria are aligned with it in both directions.
- A criterion that misstates or contradicts a marked source fails the [Correct](../references/requirement-characteristics.md#individual) characteristic.
- A requirement a marked source states that no criterion makes true, and no Non-Goal excludes, is a gap.

- **Titles.**
- A title is a short name, a colon, and a subtitle stating the outcome.
- The name is two or three words and the subtitle a succinct summary of at most ten, in title case.
- A prefixed title separates its levels with colons, then the name.
- **Bodies.**
- Every body keeps the section order of its kind template and the columns of that kind's table.
- Fill each `{{…}}` and delete a section the template marks as optional when it has nothing to say.
- **Code references.**

A body references code as a link on the words it supports, a permalink pinned to a commit with its line anchors, never a bare `path:line`: `the [extrinsic type](…/blob/<sha>/runtime/src/lib.rs#L1231-L1232)`.
- **Succinct items.**

Each Problem and Proposal item, and each of its sub-bullets, is at most two lines. A bold opener does not count toward the two. Several distinct points go in a bulleted list, never packed into those two lines.
- **Bold leads.**
- A Problem or Proposal item that opens with a bold statement puts its body on the next line, indented under the bullet:
- A bulleted item with sub-bullets keeps the line introducing them on its bold statement's line:
- **Labels.**
- Add `enhancement`, `bug` and `tech-debt` as they apply.
- **Example.**  workflow-server adds `workflows`.
- Only labels that exist are applied.
- **Friction.**
A Problem states the friction as it is now. Its evidence is a count or a code link for that friction. A Problem does not describe the plan.
- **Plan ids.**
A Problem or Proposal names no epic, task or acceptance criterion of its own initiative. The Work Breakdown table holds those references; a sibling boundary is plain language.
- **Evidence that may be cited.**
Code, a merged pull request, and an issue outside this initiative may be cited.
An acceptance criterion meets these. A kind adds its own under its Acceptance Criteria.
- States an end state, not an activity.
- Names or implies the instrument that observes it: a test, a guard, a command or a measure.
- Is unambiguous, so two readers agree on whether it holds.
- Meets [Requirement Characteristics](../references/requirement-characteristics.md).
- **One invariant.**
Each criterion states a single condition that holds or does not. One joining several is split, and the Coverage cells cite the new ones. A condition over a list of subjects is one condition.

Criteria are labelled `AC1` onward, in ascending order. A criterion that leaves a body takes its label with it, and the criteria that remain keep theirs, since other work cites them, so the labels may ascend with a gap.
- Subjective wording is an observable pass or fail, or the criterion is absent.
- A fact that inspection, analysis, demonstration, or test can check is kept, such as every option having a description.
- A judgment about meaning, such as a claim that a description states what choosing means, is subjective wording.
- An item none of those methods can observe is named as [Coverage Reports](#coverage-reports) define, and it stays named there.
- **Done.**
The last column. Its cell is empty while the row is open, and a tick, ✓, when the row is complete.
- **Description.**
A short phrase naming what the row delivers, at most eight words, with no list, semicolon or detail.
- **Coverage.**
The acceptance criteria the row delivers, `AC2, AC5`, and nothing else. Every criterion is delivered by at least one row.
- **Depends on.**
References only, with no prose, and only what no other entry in the cell already implies.
Rows are numbered in the order they can start, so every dependency points to an earlier row. Numbering that does not follow start order is advisory.
Work a pull request names keeps its number. Renumbering touches only a row no pull request names.
Tables write references with colons, the form the scripts read. Prose uses a space.
- **Stale references.**
A row number, issue link or decision wording agrees with the current plan.
- **Body.**
A body states the plan as it is. It carries no change narrative. How the plan evolved belongs in the planning record and in commit and pull request bodies.
Task and epic numbers, issue links and wording must agree with the current decisions and bodies. References to superseded decisions are findings.
An issue's References section does not link issues or pull requests on the same board. A public issue's References cite public repositories; unavailable visibility is unresolved.
- **Unobservable items.**
An item a test cannot observe is named in the plan or the coverage report. It stays in the report.
- **The check matches the criterion.**
- A file or string check counts as coverage only when the criterion is a fact about that file.
- A criterion about a run is covered by a run that shows it.
- **The specified set.**
A coverage report lists every acceptance criterion the work under review is specified to cover.
- **Fixed.**
Structural changes preserve the wording and are present in the returned body file, with a body diff.
- **Apply.** Title or label changes for the caller to publish on the issue.
- **Decide.** Missing content or a judgement for the caller to resolve.

- A pull request's title starts with the epic it works on: `[I07:E00] Purpose`.
- A hot-fix's pull request takes the title its [Delivering Pull Request](hotfix.md#delivering-pull-request) names.
- A pull request working on neither an epic nor a hot-fix takes `Name: Subtitle`, with no prefix, as a revision of the skill itself does.
- The prefix is how an epic's pull requests are found, and each one, open or merged, is matched to the tasks it works on from its changes and the tasks' Descriptions.
- The pull request that merges an epic base carries the same prefix. Its head is the epic base, which tells it from a task pull request.
- A title carrying an initiative's prefix names one of its epics. An epic sync reports one that names none as `no epic`, and one naming its epic by a task id, `[I07:E00:W01]`, as `retitle`.
- Overview is one paragraph on what the base carries.
- Changes holds one heading per area, with a bullet per functional change.

- A Changes bullet states what the base does and carries no count of the corpus, such as how many specifications or files it holds. A count belongs in the unit's planning record, with the revision that produced it.
- Each file a Changes bullet names in a code span stands at the base's head. A code name, such as `board.Outputs`, names no file.
- References cites each task pull request merged into that base.
- It carries no Test Plan, since it delivers no task of its own, and no statement about what the epic has yet to deliver. The epic's Work Breakdown is where delivery state is read.
A task pull request carries a Test Plan.
- **Table.**
The pull request's Test Plan section contains only one table, with columns Test, Description, Coverage and Pass, in that order.
- **Columns.**
- Test names the id.
- Description briefly names the check.
- Coverage names the criteria the check observes, `AC1, AC3`, and is empty when the check observes none.
- A row whose Test cell is empty names a criterion no check observes, and its Pass cell is empty.
- Pass is empty while a check awaits a result. A recorded result uses ✓ when the check ran and held, or an accurate label such as Partial, Fail or Not run.
- **Evidence.**
- Test procedures, tested revisions, observations, limitations and supporting evidence belong in the work's published planning document.
- Each recorded result in Pass links to its relevant section in that document, using the result as link text: `[✓](URL#check)` or `[Partial](URL#check)`.
- Each evidence link is accessible to the pull request's readers and resolves to the intended section.
- **Completion.**
The test plan has passed when every row with a Test id carries ✓ as its result. Partial, failed and unexecuted checks remain incomplete.

- Every criterion a unit's Coverage names has an observing test in its work item and pull request. A criterion no test can observe remains in the [coverage report](issue-body.md#coverage-reports) and in a test-plan row with an empty Test cell.

- The criterion selects the test kind: a unit test for one component, an integration test for a seam between components, and an end-to-end or system test for running-system behaviour. That evidence meets [Coverage Reports](issue-body.md#coverage-reports).
- An instrument that does not exist yet is work the task carries, as the verified rule defines. Use the project's own system test where it can observe the criterion.
- One row per check, in execution order, followed by any unobserved criteria. Every criterion in the unit's Coverage appears in at least one row.
